slides.title: Where it already lives
steps: The access layer assumes not every port transmits at once.
The uplink assumes not every switch bursts together.
The circuit assumes a fraction of what the LAN could generate.

slides.title: Not a trick
slides.body:
Nobody snuck it past you.
It's what makes the network
*affordable*.

slides.title: Zero contention
slides.body:
Buying capacity the business
will *never use* —
and defending it every budget cycle.

slides.title: The real problem
slides.body:
In most estates,
nobody can tell you
*what the ratio is*.

Somebody chose 20 to 1.
For reasons that made sense
with *2019's* traffic.

slides.title: Then
slides.body:
Video became constant.
A backup moved into hours.
Three sites started replicating.

slides.title: The ratio didn't change
slides.body:
The thing it was
a *bet about* did.

slides.title: The question
slides.body:
What ratio did you choose?
What did it assume?
When was that *last checked*?

slides.title:
A ratio nobody remembers
agreeing to is a *liability*.
slides.body:
One that happens
to be working.
